notes: Summary model-stop: selected gpt-5.6-sol, removed temperature, and replaced max_tokens with a completion budget that also accommodates reasoning.
Vision model-stop: selected gpt-4o and replaced max_tokens with max_completion_tokens while preserving image input and response parsing.
Speech model-stop: replaced the speech HTTP request with gpt-realtime-2.1-mini over WebSocket; PCM events are collected into WAV, and the playback MIME type now matches.
WelcomeForm GPT-3.5 model-unresolved: both the selection and active-state comparison now use gpt-5.6-terra; signed configuration carries that selection into Responses.
runAssistant model-unresolved: removed the o3-mini override and honor the verified assistant configuration, including gpt-5.6-sol.
WelcomeForm GPT-4 model-unresolved: both the selection and active-state comparison now use gpt-5.6-sol, with an updated label.
Transcription model-unresolved: the multipart request now sends gpt-transcribe and explicitly requests the JSON text response consumed by the route.
addMessage SDK-major: upgraded to OpenAI 6 and compatible Zod 3; message insertion now uses Conversation items.
checkRunStatus SDK-major: upgraded to OpenAI 6; polling now retrieves a stored Response and validates its Conversation.
createAssistant SDK-major: upgraded to OpenAI 6; replaced remote assistant creation with authenticated portable configuration and indexed vector-store files.
createThread SDK-major: upgraded to OpenAI 6; creates a Conversation while retaining the threadId response field expected by clients.
listMessages SDK-major: upgraded to OpenAI 6; retrieves paginated Conversation items and extracts assistant output text.
runAssistant SDK-major: upgraded to OpenAI 6; creates a background Response with Conversation state, instructions, and optional hosted file search.
addMessage legacy-endpoint review: removed the retired message endpoint and preserved the existing request/response contract.
checkRunStatus legacy-endpoint review: removed run retrieval; maps incomplete Responses to a terminal failure and returns errors rather than falling through.

createAssistant legacy-endpoint review: removed assistant creation and obsolete retrieval configuration. Signed configuration avoids dashboard provisioning and process-local storage; existing retired assistant IDs must be recreated. Keep ASSISTANT_CONFIG_SECRET stable across deployments, or signing defaults to OPENAI_API_KEY.
createThread legacy-endpoint review: removed thread creation; the initial user message is stored in the new Conversation.
listMessages legacy-endpoint review: removed thread message listing; newest assistant text or refusal is returned using the existing messages string field.

runAssistant legacy-endpoint review: removed run creation. Hosted file search handles the only configured tool, so no custom function-call loop is required. Background Responses preserve the existing runId/polling workflow.

patterns.item: A model replacement also required removing an unsupported sampling control and revising the output-token budget.
A multimodal model replacement required reviewing the token-limit parameter rather than changing only the model string.
A binary speech request needed conversion to an event-driven audio protocol with different output framing.
A model selected through interface state reached the provider only through a later configuration request.
A model embedded in a legacy execution options object needed migration together with the surrounding execution lifecycle.
A model choice was duplicated between an interface event handler and its selected-state comparison.
A multipart form hid the model selection from direct SDK request tracing.

findings.summary: Calls the Assistants API, which OpenAI shut down on 2026-08-26, so these requests fail today. The move is not one-to-one: assistants become Prompts (configured in the dashboard), threads become Conversations, runs become Responses, and the tool-call loop moves into your code. Refit lists each call for review and does not rewrite it.

Refit lists each call for review and does not rewrite it.

notes: src/index.ts:37 — Appends to server-side thread history; a Responses request cannot faithfully replace this operation.
src/openai/createAssistant.ts:7 — Creates and returns a persistent Assistant used by downstream runs. Responses cannot preserve that object and ID contract.
src/openai/createRun.ts:9 — Creates a run using an existing thread and assistant ID; migration requires changing state management and the Run contract.
src/openai/createRun.ts:16 — Polls an Assistants Run; Responses cannot retrieve that run or preserve its lifecycle.
src/openai/createThread.ts:5 — Creates and returns a server-side Thread; Responses cannot preserve the Thread contract.
src/openai/createThread.ts:8 — Stores the initial message in an OpenAI thread; replacement requires migrating conversation state.
src/openai/handleRunToolCalls.ts:43 — Submits tool outputs to an existing Assistants Run. Responses requires a different tool-call continuation flow and return contract.
src/openai/performRun.ts:17 — Persists an assistant error message in thread history; a generation request would not preserve this behavior.
src/openai/performRun.ts:30 — Reads stored thread messages; response.output_text cannot replace thread-history retrieval.

patterns.item: A chat loop depended on persistent remote thread state and passed remote assistant identities between helpers.
Remote assistant creation returned a persistent resource whose identity and nested tool schema were consumed downstream.
Run creation depended on two remote resource identities rather than self-contained generation configuration.
An asynchronous run lifecycle required status polling that does not map directly to synchronous generation.
Conversation state was created through a legacy persistent thread resource.
Initial user messages were inserted separately into a newly created legacy state container.
Tool execution depended on run-specific required actions and a server-managed submission-and-poll lifecycle.
Failure handling wrote synthetic assistant messages into legacy server-side history.
Final output was selected from historical assistant messages rather than from the current generation.
Interactive message insertion was coupled to legacy state types and downstream orchestration.
Persistent assistant configuration had to become inline generation settings or an externally configured prompt.
Generation creation required coordinated changes to configuration ownership and conversation references.
Repeated run retrieval encoded lifecycle semantics absent from the replacement synchronous call.
A helper exposed a legacy remote state type across module boundaries.
Optional initial history used a legacy message insertion shape tied to a newly created state resource.
Tool results used legacy submission identifiers instead of continuation input items correlated with function calls.
Error presentation depended on persisting locally generated text as a remote assistant message.
Response extraction depended on listing shared history after a separate run lifecycle completed.

notes: Line 133: Assistant creation belongs to a thread-based workflow; left unchanged with the file.
Line 141: Stores the destination prompt in an OpenAI thread.
Line 146: Runs the destination assistant against server-side thread messages.
Line 152: Retrieves thread message content for destination parsing.
Line 220: Assistant creation belongs to the thread-based flight workflow.
Line 228: Stores the flight prompt in an OpenAI thread.
Line 233: Runs the flight assistant against server-side thread messages.
Line 243: Retrieves thread content blocks used in the returned flight results.
Line 322: Assistant creation belongs to the thread-based hotel workflow.
Line 330: Stores the hotel prompt in an OpenAI thread.
Line 335: Runs the hotel assistant against server-side thread messages.
Line 342: Retrieves an Assistants text block used by the existing hotel parser.
Line 390: Assistant creation belongs to the final thread-based hotel workflow.
Line 398: Stores the final hotel prompt in an OpenAI thread.
Line 403: Runs the final hotel assistant against server-side thread messages.
Line 413: Retrieves Assistants content blocks returned by the function.
Line 437: Assistant creation belongs to the thread-based activity workflow.
Line 445: Stores the activity prompt in an OpenAI thread.
Line 450: Runs the activity assistant against server-side thread messages.
Line 459: Retrieves thread content blocks used in the returned activity results.
Line 536: Assistant creation belongs to the thread-based itinerary workflow.
Line 544: Stores the itinerary prompt in an OpenAI thread.
Line 549: Runs the itinerary assistant against server-side thread messages.
Line 556: Retrieves thread message content for itinerary parsing.
Line 637: Returns a server-created Thread object; Responses or Chat Completions cannot preserve that return contract.

stops.reason: The AI left this site unchanged: src/assistant/assistant.service.ts: Left unchanged under the thread-state exception. Although each workflow creates a fresh thread, it stores prompts server-side and subsequently runs and retrieves messages from that thread. The public threadConversation() method also returns the actual Thread object. Preserving that output contract is not possible using client.responses.create or client.chat.completions.create within the permitted edits.

notes: Fine-tuning creation now uses gpt-5.6-terra and conversational JSONL rather than legacy prompt/completion records.
The text chat branch uses gpt-4.1, preserving the existing Chat Completions message and response shapes.
Image variations now use images.edit with a variation instruction, PNG uploads, supported dimensions and base64 response decoding.
Image generation uses gpt-image-2, medium/high quality and supported dimensions; the saved visual style is expressed in the prompt.

Speech now uses the Realtime WebSocket API with gpt-realtime-2.1-mini. PCM output is encoded to Ogg/Opus for Telegram using ffmpeg-static. Legacy voice choices are mapped where necessary, and the obsolete quality selector is hidden. Realtime read-aloud behavior is not guaranteed to be verbatim TTS.
The retired fine-tuned classifier is no longer hardcoded. Its test method requires an explicitly configured, newly trained model; no unfine-tuned substitute is silently used.
The vision chat branch now uses gpt-4o with the existing image message format.
The OpenAI dependency is upgraded to major 6; WebSocket and audio-encoding dependencies support the speech migration.
Legacy Completions inference is replaced by Responses input and output_text handling. The original call used none of suffix, echo, best_of or logprobs.

rules.summary: Moves the openai package to the newest 6.x release. 6.x has no runtime dependencies; 7.0.0 only adds a Node.js 22 requirement, which Refit does not impose on a repository.
`beta.chat.completions.parse` moved to `chat.completions.parse` in v5.

notes: No patch proposed: a safe migration requires coordinated changes to conversation creation, message storage, response generation, tool execution, assistant configuration, and dependencies. Several essential files were omitted.
SocketEmitController.ts:72 — Conversation retrieval must be migrated together with persisted thread IDs; the file was omitted.
SocketEmitController.ts:81 — Message creation requires content and attachment conversion; the file was omitted.
ThreadController.ts:177 — Changing creation alone would produce conversation IDs that the existing run and message helpers cannot consume.
ThreadController.ts:197 — Message creation depends on the unavailable formatter and message-history implementation.
ThreadController.ts:269 — Conversation copying must preserve message ordering, roles, attachments, and supported content types.
ThreadController.ts:329 — Existing persisted thread IDs cannot simply be passed to conversation retrieval.
ThreadController.ts:349 — The asynchronous formatter also needs to be awaited, but its implementation is needed to determine the correct replacement payload.
WorkspaceController.ts:142 — Assistant provisioning must be replaced with application configuration or dashboard Prompt references; the file was omitted.
mock.ts:56 — Seed provisioning must use the same replacement configuration as workspace creation; the file was omitted.
checkRunStatus.ts:11 — Active-run discovery needs a replacement response-ID persistence and concurrency strategy.
checkRunStatus.ts:25 — Response retrieval cannot safely replace run retrieval while callers still pass run IDs.
checkRunStatus.ts:32 — Message retrieval must migrate with the history formatter and token-accounting consumer.
checkRunStatus.ts:91 — Tool execution must move into a Responses continuation loop that submits function-call outputs.
checkThread.ts:15 — Conversation creation must migrate together with every consumer of the saved ID.
checkThread.ts:34 — Replacement conversation creation has the same coordination requirement as initial creation.
vision.ts:17 — Vision accounting needs the configured replacement model rather than an assistant lookup.
openai.ts:20 — No replacement Prompt references, assistant configuration exports, or model configuration were supplied.
openai.ts:49 — Response generation must preserve configured instructions, tools, retrieval resources, and accounting behavior.
openai.ts:68 — Usage accounting must consume Responses usage rather than an Assistants run.
createAssistant.ts:11 — The provisioning implementation was omitted.
retrieveAssistant.ts:5 — Replacement configuration storage and its callers are needed before removing this lookup.
updateAssistant.ts:11 — The configuration-update implementation was omitted.
listMessages.ts:7 — The message-history implementation was omitted.
The package manifest and lockfile were not supplied, so neither the OpenAI major-version upgrade nor the reported pnpm importer mismatch can be patched with exact edits.

+# Responses runner migration
+
+The runner now uses the Responses API and requires OpenAI SDK 6.x. Install dependencies and commit the generated lockfile.
+
+## Required deployment setup
+
+1. Create a dashboard Prompt for each former assistant. Copy its instructions and select the appropriate available model in the dashboard; no model is hard-coded by this migration.
+2. Configure its function tools using Responses function-tool definitions. Preserve the existing parameter schemas for `communitateToAgent` (`message`, `type`), `searchGoogle` (`query`), and `fetchURL` (`url`). The corrected spelling `communicateToAgent` is also supported. Preserve the original allowed agent types; they cannot be inferred from the runner.
+3. Create a Conversation for each chat and store its `conv_` ID instead of a legacy thread ID. Add user messages through Conversation items before invoking the runner. Import any previously exported history that must be retained; legacy thread IDs are not conversation IDs.
+4. Pass the conversation ID and dashboard `pmpt_` ID to `startRun(conversationId, promptId)`. Any direct `processRun` caller must now supply a Response, conversation ID and prompt ID. Update nested agent invocations in the same way.
+
+The runner deliberately rejects legacy IDs rather than silently starting a new chat without its history or instructions. Existing assistant configuration, conversation creation/message-writing code, and stored thread mappings were not included in the migration input, so their deployment migration must be completed separately.
+
+The runner executes function calls locally and submits their results to the same conversation until a final message is available. It returns `null` if there is no final message; otherwise it returns an object with `id`, `role`, and text-compatible `content` entries (`content[i].text.value`). This is not a full legacy Thread Message: consumers needing other legacy fields must be updated. Text annotations are now Responses annotations. Failed or incomplete responses throw rather than being mistaken for successful replies.

+speech_file_path = "AI_speech.wav"
+text = "我是咖哥，可能你有所不知，我拥有两个美少女助理，一个是小冰，一个是小雪!"
+
+
+def synthesize_speech(text, output_path):
+    # Realtime输出PCM音频；使用WAV容器，不将PCM数据误标为MP3。
+    with closing(create_connection(
+        "wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime?model=gpt-realtime-2.1-mini",
+        header=[f"Authorization: Bearer {os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY']}"],
+        timeout=60,
+    )) as connection:
+        connection.send(json.dumps({
+            "type": "session.update",
+            "session": {
+                "type": "realtime",
+                "output_modalities": ["audio"],
+                "audio": {
+                    "output": {
+                        "format": {"type": "audio/pcm", "rate": 24000},
+                        "voice": "alloy",
+                    }
+                },
+            },
+        }))
+        audio = bytearray()
+        while True:
+            raw_event = connection.recv()
+            if not raw_event:
+                raise RuntimeError("Realtime connection closed before speech completed")
+            event = json.loads(raw_event)
+            event_type = event.get("type")
+            if event_type == "error":
+                raise RuntimeError(f"Realtime error: {event.get('error')}")
+            if event_type == "session.updated":
+                connection.send(json.dumps({
+                    "type": "conversation.item.create",
+                    "item": {
+                        "type": "message",
+                        "role": "user",
+                        "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": text}],
+                    },
+                }))
+                connection.send(json.dumps({
+                    "type": "response.create",
+                    "response": {
+                        "instructions": "Read the user's text aloud verbatim. Do not add any other words.",
+                    },
+                }))
+            elif event_type == "response.output_audio.delta":
+                audio.extend(base64.b64decode(event["delta"]))
+            elif event_type == "response.done":
+                response = event["response"]
+                if response.get("status") != "completed":
+                    raise RuntimeError(f"Speech generation failed: {response.get('status_details')}")
+                if not audio:
+                    raise RuntimeError("Speech generation returned no audio")
+                break
+
+    with wave.open(output_path, "wb") as output:
+        output.setnchannels(1)
+        output.setsampwidth(2)
+        output.setframerate(24000)
+        output.writeframes(audio)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    synthesize_speech(text, speech_file_path)

+import asyncio
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, patch
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel
+
+from wandbot.models.llm import AsyncOpenAILLMModel
+
+
+class JudgeOutput(BaseModel):
+    reason: str
+
+
+def make_model(model_name, response_model=None):
+    with patch("wandbot.models.llm.AsyncOpenAI") as client_class:
+        model = AsyncOpenAILLMModel(
+            model_name=model_name,
+            temperature=0.1,
+            response_model=response_model,
+        )
+    return model, client_class.return_value
+
+
+def test_replacement_models_structured_outputs():
+    async def run():
+        for name in ("gpt-6-luna", "gpt-5.6-sol", "gpt-5.6-terra"):
+            model, client = make_model(name, JudgeOutput)
+            expected = JudgeOutput(reason="Correct")
+            client.beta.chat.completions.parse = AsyncMock(
+                return_value=SimpleNamespace(
+                    choices=[SimpleNamespace(message=SimpleNamespace(parsed=expected))]
+                )
+            )
+            messages = [{"role": "system", "content": "Judge the answer."}]
+            result, status = await model.create(messages)
+            assert status.success
+            assert result == expected
+            params = client.beta.chat.completions.parse.call_args.kwargs
+            assert params["model"] == name
+            assert "temperature" not in params
+            assert params["response_format"] is JudgeOutput
+            assert params["messages"][0]["role"] == "developer"
+            assert messages == [{"role": "system", "content": "Judge the answer."}]
+
+    asyncio.run(run())
+
+
+def test_replacement_model_plain_text():
+    async def run():

+                choices=[SimpleNamespace(message=SimpleNamespace(content="Translation"))]
+            )
+        )
+        result, status = await model.create([{"role": "user", "content": "Translate"}])
+        assert status.success
+        assert result == "Translation"
+        params = client.chat.completions.create.call_args.kwargs
+        assert params["model"] == "gpt-6-luna"
+        assert "temperature" not in params
+        assert "response_format" not in params
+
+    asyncio.run(run())
